why: Stored 09:00 open was a half-hour early. Carousel Craft Shows is the promoter, and its own page for this show prints "Date(s)/Time: / December 12, 2026 / 9:30 AM - 4:00 PM" with the year explicit, plus "Maple Grove Community Center / 12951 Weaver Lake Road / Maple Grove, MN 55369" and "Admission: Free". Read twice by independent routes (WebFetch and the browser pane's raw page text) and they agree string for string. The stored 16:00 close already matches the printed "4:00 PM" and is quoted, not derived from a running time, so it stands. Date, venue, city and the Free tier were all already right. Citation moves off a blog roundup (givemethemike.com) onto the organiser; the roundup's 9:30 happened to be correct but a blog cannot confirm anything on its own. No span: the organiser's own /shows/ index prints one date per show, so no Sunday half-day exists anywhere on its site. No title change - the organiser's heading says "... 2026" and thecraftmap calls it the "13th", but both would rewrite event_key for no reader benefit, and the ordinal is unattested.

Stored 19:30 is wrong. The Dakota's own event page for this occurrence heads the date "Dec 7 | Mon" and prints one showtime, "7:00 PM"; the same page's JSON-LD gives startDate 2026-12-07T19:00:00-06:00, and the venue's December iCal prints DTSTART;TZID=America/Chicago:20261207T190000 against SUMMARY:Asleep At the Wheel with this same permalink. This is NOT a missed second seating: the same page lists Nov 4 at both "7:00 PM" and "9:30 PM" as separate lines, so double seatings do render when they exist, and the Dakota IS on the two-seatings allowlist in lib/contradictions.ts - it is simply not in play on this night. The stored 22:30 end is cleared rather than moved: the only end figure anywhere is an identical two-hour DTEND/endDate of 21:00 on BOTH nights, the signature of a calendar-plugin default, never printed to a reader. Clearing beats inventing. NO STAMP, deliberately: the start is fully quoted, but choosing "no end" over the organiser's own machine-readable 21:00 is judgement rather than a quote, so this row takes the free re-check instead. Citation moves off the venue's index calendar onto the page for this specific show. NOT FIXABLE HERE, for the record: the page prints "From $74.91" and there is no price field, and the Dakota plays a SECOND NIGHT, Tue 8 Dec 2026 at 7:00 PM, which we do not carry at all - a correction cannot add a row.

Stored 12:00 start was wrong and the 14:30 end was a 2.5-hour expansion off that wrong start. The organiser's own 2026-27 women's basketball schedule prints the Indiana row as "vs / Indiana / The Barn by Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Minnesota / Radio: 96.7 KFAN+ / Big Ten Home Opener / Jan 2 / (Sat) / 5:00 PM". "Indiana" occurs exactly once in the whole page: one Indiana game all season, at home, on Jan 2, so the sports rule is not engaged and there is no away game to confuse this row with. The year is attested rather than extrapolated - the page heading reads "2026-27 Women's Basketball Schedule" and the row's Game Center page carries the organiser's own title "Women's Basketball vs Indiana on 1/2/2027" - and 2027-01-02 is independently a Saturday, matching the printed "(Sat)". Venue is not an error: the row's venue link resolves to the organiser's own Williams Arena facility page, so The Barn and Williams Arena are one building and title, venue, city and pin are untouched. The end is CLEARED, not re-derived: the organiser publishes no finish time for any game, and a basketball running time is not a source. Citation moves off ESPN, which raised the flag; its 17:00 agreed, but the organiser is what settles it.

The worst shape in this batch, and worse than the flag described: stored start 2026-12-26 10:00 with end 2027-01-03 17:00, which is a NINE-DAY span under lib/dates.ts daysSpanned, so this single row has been printing a 10:00 performance on all nine day pages from 26 Dec to 3 Jan - on a production we already carry as individual dated performances. CTC's own page for the 26-27 run prints "Saturday / Dec 26 / 11:00am" and "Saturday / Dec 26 / 2:00pm" as two separately ticketed performances (distinct ticket URLs), so 10:00-to-3-Jan was two performances plus dead air flattened into one. This row becomes the day's FIRST performance, 11:00. The end is CLEARED, not set: the page prints no finish time for any performance, only "1 hour and 50 minutes with one 15-minute intermission", and deriving 13:05 from a running time is inventing an end. The year is attested on the same page - the calendar entries print no year but the range line reads "November 3, 2026-January 3, 2027", and 26 Dec is a Saturday in 2026 and was a Friday in 2025, so the year-shift shape that produced the last fabrication batch is ruled out. NO SPAN, deliberately: six sibling rows already list this production's individual performances (3, 4, 7, 14 and 26 Nov), so a span here would double-list it, and making this row the run would need start 2026-11-03, a past date that rewrites event_key. Citation moves off the venue's index calendar onto the production's own page. NOT FIXABLE HERE: the organiser prints "$25.00 - $105.00" and there is no price field.

Stored start was 00:00, an all-day placeholder and not a performance time, with the run's last day stuffed into end_at as 2026-12-24 23:59. Penumbra's own dated schedule prints "Tuesday, December 1, 2026 | 7:30PM" under "Remaining dates & tickets" - year and weekday printed, and 1 Dec 2026 is independently a Tuesday - so the start becomes 19:30. The end is CLEARED: the page says "Running time: TBA" in so many words and prints no curtain-down time anywhere, so any finish would be invented. The span moves into the column that is actually for it: the page's banner reads "December 1 - December 24" and its last dated line is "Thursday, December 24, 2026 | 2:00PM", so multi_day_end becomes 2026-12-24. One production, one organiser URL, one author and director - a theatre run, not the separately-ticketed-nights shape that Wobbleween was - and it is the only Black Nativity row we hold, so nothing is double-listed. All 23 printed performance lines were checked against the 2026 calendar: every weekday matches and the dark days fall on Mon 7, Tue 8, Mon 14 and Mon 21, which is a real theatre run rather than a generated list. At 24 days the span exceeds EXPAND_MAX_DAYS, so per fc23f93 this shows on 1 December plus /ongoing, exactly as it does today - the rendering does not change, only the honesty of the start time and of which column carries the run. Citation moves off a seasonal "101 ideas for holiday family fun" listicle, whose content is replaced under a stable URL every year, onto the organiser's own overview page, which carries every verify-relevant value on one page and spells the venue and city the way we store them. Cite the penumbracenter.org host: penumbratheatre.org 302-redirects. NOT PROVEN, so not acted on: the page gives two different run starts - the banner and schedule begin 1 December, the prose body says "December 3 through December 24, 2026" - and the word "preview" appears nowhere, so 1-2 December cannot be called previews. Our row's date is attested either way, because Penumbra sells tickets for Tue 1 Dec 7:30PM.

Stored 19:30 start with end 2026-12-24 21:30, which is a three-day span, so this row prints a 19:30 Cirque performance on 23 and 24 December as well. We cited the venue index, which in a real browser prints only "Cirque Dreams Holidaze / December 22 - 24" with no time and no year. The show's own organiser page is at a slug we were not using and lists four separately ticketed performances under a "Performances" heading: "Tuesday, December 22 at 7 PM", "Wednesday, December 23 at 3 PM", "Wednesday, December 23 at 7 PM", "Thursday, December 24 at 11 AM". Ours is the 22 Dec show, so the start is 19:00, not 19:30. Hennepin Arts' own press release, datelined "MINNEAPOLIS (Aug. 14, 2026)", prints the identical schedule in a DAY/DATE/TIME table - two organiser pages agreeing is a finding, not a question. The end is CLEARED: neither organiser page prints a finish or a running time, so 21:30 was invented. NO SPAN, and this is the one place I differ from the research pass that wrote this batch: its reason was that separately ticketed performances at different clock times are not one run, which would also have ruled out Black Nativity above. The real reason is the cap. A three-day span renders on all three day pages carrying ONE start time, so a span here would print "7:00 PM" on 24 December, whose only performance is 11 AM - a wrong time stated as fact. Black Nativity's 24-day run exceeds EXPAND_MAX_DAYS and therefore shows on its start day only, where a span can print no wrong time. An omission beats a wrong time, so this row stays a single dated performance. The cost is real and is reported rather than papered over: 23 and 24 December lose their only Cirque listing until the three missing performances are carried as their own rows, which a correction cannot do. Citation moves to the show's own page. DO NOT use the bare /events/cirque-dreams-holidaze slug - it is live but serves the ended 2024 engagement ("December 20 - 22, 2024", "This event has ended"); no other row of ours cites it, checked.

Stored 19:00 is wrong. The organiser's live schedule, under the heading "2026-27 Women's Hockey Schedule", prints "vs / Minnesota Duluth / Ridder Arena / Minneapolis, MN / Jan 15 / (Fri) / 6:00 PM", with the year in that row's own markup as 2027-01-15T18:00:00, and its ticket link carries the UTC stamp 2027-01-16T00:00:00Z, which is the same instant. 15 Jan 2027 is a Friday, matching the printed "(Fri)" and our stored date, so only the clock moves. An independent check inside our own calendar: the organiser's next row is "Jan 16 / (Sat) / 2:00 PM" and our Game 2 row already stores 2027-01-16 14:00, so the page agrees with us on the night we had right and disagrees on the one we had wrong. Venue, city and home-away all match, so the pin stays and "(Game 1)" remains positionally correct - though it is our label, not the organiser's. The 21:00 end is CLEARED, not re-derived: the page prints no finish time for any game. Citation moves off the May 2026 announcement, which prints "Jan. 15-16 - vs. Minnesota Duluth" and no clock time anywhere on it - so the flag's 18:00 could not have come from the page it named, however right the number turns out to be. KNOWN LIMIT: gophersports.com is JS-rendered, so neither the old nor the new citation can be read by the weekly scripted check; the move costs no machine-readability but gains none either, and this row may well come back flagged.

The only DATE error in this batch, and a three-day one: stored 2027-01-18, which is a Monday. Treasure Island's own event page prints "Friday, January 15, 8pm" and "when the legendary acts team up in the Island Event Center on Friday, January 15!", with the year on that same page three ways that agree - the entry's own element, time class="event-item__date" datetime="2027-01-15CST20:00:00" whose text content IS the visible "Friday, January 15, 8:00PM"; the schema.org block naming "JEFFERSON STARSHIP AND JOHN WAITE" with startDate "2027-01-15CST20:00:00-21600"; and the entry's position in the venue's live chronological list, immediately after "Thursday, December 31, 7:00PM". The printed weekday is an independent lock: 15 Jan is a Friday in 2027, a Thursday in 2026 and a Saturday in 2028. All 14 dated entries in that list were checked against the calendar and all 14 weekdays are correct, including the CST-to-CDT flip at the right date in March 2027 - a live, chronological, weekday-correct venue calendar attesting its own year. The 23:00 end is CLEARED, not moved: the organiser prints no finish and no doors time, and its JSON-LD endDate is byte-identical to its startDate, which attests nothing. Checked before applying, because a date change rewrites event_key and event_key is unique across every status: there is NO other row on 2027-01-15 and no other Jefferson Starship or John Waite row of any status, so this is a safe re-key rather than a duplicate. Citation moves off a Songkick metal genre index, which is an aggregator and the wrong genre besides. Title and venue deliberately NOT "fixed" to the organiser's "JEFFERSON STARSHIP AND JOHN WAITE" and "Island Event Center": both feed event_key, the room is inside the property so the pin and city are already right, and re-keying twice for cosmetics is how a duplicate gets made. Resale aggregators list this date as Jefferson Starship alone without Waite; the organiser names both in its title and its JSON-LD performer, so the aggregators are wrong, not the venue.
